title: Variant Staged Rollout Governance and Customer Experiment Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook defines governance, experiment design, customer communication, and operational safeguards for staged rollouts of model variants and serving fidelity changes across Redwood deployment surfaces (hosted API, Dedicated, Private). It is intended for product managers, release engineers, SRE, solutions engineering, and account teams running controlled experiments with customers or launching variant SKUs.

Goals

- Provide a repeatable, low-risk process for rolling out model variants (architecture, quantization, tokenization changes) and fidelity packages to production customers.
- Ensure customer-facing experiments are safe, measurable, and reversible.
- Align launch decisions with economics (cost delta), latency SLOs, and quality regression tolerance.

Scope and Definitions

- Variant: any model binary or serving configuration that changes inference behavior (e.g., quantized v2, distilled-512, attention-optimized kernel build).
- Fidelity package: a bundled runtime configuration that trades off latency/cost for output quality (e.g., Fidelity-High, Fidelity-Balanced, Fidelity-Lite).
- Experiment: a customer or tenant-scoped A/B or phased exposure used to measure business and technical impact.

Applicable surfaces:
- hosted-inference (public API)
- dedicated-pool (reserved GPU capacity)
- private-deploy (VPC / on-prem bundles)

Principles and Governance

1. Safety-first: any rollout must have an automated fallback path and a clear rollback trigger set before customer exposure.
2. Metric-driven: decisions are based on pre-defined statistical tests on quality, latency, cost, and reliability signals.
3. Customer transparency: accounts in experiments receive pre-launch documentation and post-experiment summary.
4. Least surprise: changes that affect token accounting, output format, or prompt semantics require product and solutions-eng sign-off and a migration guide.

Roles and Responsibilities

- Product Owner (PO): defines acceptance criteria, business metrics, and communicates to GTM.
- Release Lead: coordinates rollout phases, feature flags, and canary assignments.
- SRE / Runtime Owner: sets SLO thresholds, monitors telemetry, enables automatic fallback.
- Quality & Evals: provides baseline test sets, runs regression analysis, and approves quality thresholds.
- Solutions Engineering / CSM: onboards customers into experiments, documents expectations, and collects qualitative feedback.

Experiment Design: required artifacts

Every staged rollout MUST include the following artifacts before first customer exposure: 

1) Experiment Charter (one-pager): scope, hypothesis, key metrics, owner, and duration.
2) Acceptance Criteria: pass/fail thresholds for quality, latency, error rate, and cost. (see table below)
3) Test Plan & Eval Set: seed prompts and dataset mirroring customer intents; expected golden outputs where possible.
4) Rollout Plan: list of tenants/customers, assignment buckets, phasing timeline, and feature-flag IDs.
4) Communication Plan: pre-launch notice, in-experiment check-ins cadence, and post-mortem / results package template.

Acceptance Criteria (example thresholds)

| Metric | Target / Threshold | Measurement Window | Action if violated | Owner |
|--------|--------------------|--------------------|--------------------|-------|
| Quality (eval set accuracy / rouge / task-specific) | <= 1.0% relative drop vs. baseline OR p-value > 0.05 in A/B test | rolling 3 days, min N=2000 samples | Pause rollout, start triage | Quality & Evals |
| 95th-ile latency (production) | + <= 20% relative increase AND <= 200ms absolute | 1 hour rolling | Auto-fallback to baseline variant | SRE / Runtime |
| Error rate (5xx / runtime errors) | < 0.1% absolute | 15m rolling | Auto-fallback + paging | SRE |
| Cost per 1k tokens | <= 10% increase (adjusted for fidelity) | billing day | PO review; commercial approval for >10% | Finance/Product |
| Token accounting / billing parity | No unexplained token deltas | daily | Hold rollout; finance review | Billing |

Rollout Phases and Operational Steps

Phase A — Internal Canary (0% external traffic)
- Duration: minimum 48h.
- Scope: internal test tenants and canary routing in staging and production.
- Requirements: end-to-end smoke tests, evoked prompts from eval-set, and SLO observability dashboards running.
- Go / No-Go: Quality & Evals sign-off; infra stability confirmed.

Phase B — Handful of Beta Customers (up to 5 tenants / 1% traffic)
- Duration: minimum 72h.
- Assignment: opt-in customers or invited accounts via feature-flag.
- Monitoring: hourly check-ins for first 24h, then 6-hour cadence.
- Accept criteria: experimental metrics must meet the thresholds in Acceptance Criteria.

Phase C — Gradual Ramp (1% -> 50% over configurable windows)
- Typical ramp step: double exposure every 12–24h when metrics stable.
- Safety gates: rollback if any threshold violated for a single step.

Phase D — General Availability (GA) and SKU transition
- After sustained stability (>= 7 days at >= 75% exposure) and business approvals.
- Update catalog, billing SKUs, docs, and customer migration guides.

Automated Fallbacks and Feature Flags

- Every variant must be behind a ToggleID (feature flag) with an associated rollback boolean and a timeout TTL.
- Runtime must implement per-tenant fallback routing to the nearest compatible baseline variant.
- Auto-fallback triggers: latency spike, error rate threshold breach, or quality regression detected by streaming evals.

Telemetry and Measurements

Required dashboards and alerting (templates available in dashboards-and-alerts):
- Variant vs baseline latency by route (1p/95p/99p)
- Quality delta on eval-set and customer-supplied prompt sets (daily)
- Cost delta per 1k tokens and per-request CPU/GPU utilization
- Customer-side regressions (support tickets linked to feature flags)

Statistical testing guidance:
- Use two-sided t-tests or bootstrap confidence intervals for mean differences on quality metrics; ensure minimum sample size N >= 2000 for primary metric where possible.
- For small customer experiments (N < 2000) rely on paired manual review + qualitative signals.

Customer-facing commitments and SLAs

- Beta customers must sign an experiment consent that describes possible regressions, backup plan, and pledge for rapid rollback.
- For Dedicated and Private customers, any change that alters data residency, encryption, or token accounting requires a separate compliance sign-off and a planned maintenance window.

Pricing and Commercial Considerations

- If variant increases unit cost >10%, product must propose a revised SKU or fidelity surcharge and obtain Finance approval prior to GA.
- Temporary credits may be offered to customer participants to offset risk during beta.

Launch and GTM Checklist (numbered)

1. Finalize Experiment Charter and acceptance criteria.
2. Create feature flag and confirm routing policies in Smart Routing console.
3. Provision canary infra and ensure observability dashboards are populated.
4. Share pre-launch brief with participating customers and obtain consent.
5. Execute Internal Canary; collect baseline telemetry and eval results.
6. If canary passes, enable Beta Customers per assignment plan.
7. Run ramp steps with scheduled go/no-go checkpoints.
8. After GA, publish migration guide, update product catalog, and close experiment with post-mortem.

Runbook: Immediate actions for threshold violation

- If any auto-fallback trigger fires: 1) flip rollback flag for affected tenants; 2) page Release Lead and SRE; 3) create triage ticket with tag rollout-incident; 4) notify affected customers within 60 minutes via the established comms channel.

Post-experiment Reporting Template

- Executive summary (one paragraph)
- Primary metric results vs baseline (table)
- Customer feedback summary (bulleted)
- Cost and billing impact (numbers)
- Decision recommendation (GA / iterate / abandon)

Appendix: Templates and Example CLI snippets

- Feature flag toggle (CLI):
  redwood flags set --id FF-variant-2027-11 --tenants tenant-a,tenant-b --enable true

- Canary assignment (example payload):
  {
    "route": "/v1/generate",
    "variant": "quantized-v2",
    "tenants": ["tenant-a", "internal-canary"]
  }

- Query example for variant telemetry (PromQL):
  rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{variant="quantized-v2"}[5m])

Open Questions and Next Steps

- Should we standardize a per-variant minimum commercial delta that mandates a dedicated sales motion? (PO action)
- Define a simplified path for low-risk fidelity changes (e.g., non-model config) that can skip Beta Customers with product approval.

This document will be updated as we accumulate more rollout case studies. For immediate help, contact Release Lead or Quality & Evals.
